/welcome-to-the-retro-zone/: It all began in February 2012: a new retro-computing blog, a pile of old hardware and the small matter of choosing a theme. Stand by for more! 🖥️
/sega-mega-cd-model-1-acquired/: A Sega Mega-CD Model 1 arrives from Germany and immediately gets opened up for inspection. Inside lurks a JVC Optima-5 laser, with replacements hard to find. 💿
/another-sega-mega-cd-model-1-and-more-s: Another Mega-CD, two Sega Saturns and a worrying amount of corrosion. A solder-blobbed fuse and some power-supply swapping make this a proper retro haul. 🎮
/sega-saturn-laser-tune-up-success/: A supposedly dead Sega Saturn reads games again after a tiny laser adjustment. Meanwhile, a troublesome power supply refuses to join the celebration. 🔧
/fuse-replacement-on-the-sega-mega-cd-mo: A Sega Mega-CD with a blown fuse and someone's rather creative solder bypass. Time to find a proper replacement and give that overcurrent protection another chance. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-386sx-arrival/: An Amstrad Mega PC arrives with a 386SX, a built-in Mega Drive and a nasty surprise: leaking NiCad battery corrosion. The AMD processor is a welcome consolation. 🖥️
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-repair/: A leaking NiCad battery has been chewing through an Amstrad Mega PC motherboard. Repairs get things moving, but the hard-drive controller remains a mystery. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-386sx-overview/: A tour of the Amstrad Mega PC, where a 386SX and Sega Mega Drive share one beige box. Switching between the two is fun, even while the hard drives protest. 🎮
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-486slc-upgrade-exp: Could a 33 MHz TI486SLC motherboard give an Amstrad Mega PC a speed boost? Similar boards, crucial jumper settings and plenty of questions about compatibility. 💾
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-disassembled/: An Amstrad Mega PC in pieces reveals its Mega Drive ISA card, corroded tracks and some very clever video switching. Progress at last, with plenty still to fix. 🖥️
/math-coprocessors-and-you/: An empty maths coprocessor socket is an invitation! The Amstrad Mega PC's 386SX and 486SLC boards get a closer look at ULSI chips and clock speeds. 🧮
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-controller/: A beige Amstrad Mega PC controller arrives from the UK. The SP-7 pad looks wonderfully retro, even if its unresponsive D-pad makes it less wonderful to use. 🎮
/sega-saturn-model-1-power-supply-issues: A Model 1 Sega Saturn develops a strange noise after warming up. PSU swapping narrows the suspects, but the exact fault is still refusing to confess. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-486slc-upgrade-pro: The 486SLC motherboard boots and finally recognises hard drives in the Amstrad Mega PC. Then a flat real-time clock battery brings the tinkering to a halt. 💾
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-486slc-coprocessor: The Amstrad Mega PC's 33 MHz 486SLC upgrade gets a working ULSI maths coprocessor and 16 MB of tested RAM. Now for that elusive replacement clock module! 🖥️
/sega-game-gear-before-repair-no-video-q: A Sega Game Gear with barely audible sound and no usable picture heads for repair. Could its ageing capacitors be responsible for the handheld's troubles? 🎮
/new-purchases-inbound-sega-saturns-and-: Four more Sega Saturns, another Game Gear and a stack of repair parts are on the way. Will the so-called working consoles live up to their description? 📦
/sega-saturn-external-psu-proof-of-conce: A Sega Saturn boots without its original internal power supply! The external DC experiment works as a proof of concept, but proper regulation still awaits. 🔌
/new-purchases-9-april-2012/: A Sega Nomad, Dreamcast mouse, ISA network cards and Saturn power converters join the shopping list. Also, a rather intriguing early Saturn motherboard. 📦
/scorched-earth-hot-napalm-strike/: Tiny tanks, absurd weapons and one very satisfying napalm strike. A quick visit to Scorched Earth, the classic DOS artillery game where subtlety takes a holiday. 💥
/sega-game-gear-led-backlight-mod/: A Sega Game Gear gets new capacitors and an experimental LED backlight. The screen glows again, but uneven lighting and awkward repairs bring mixed results. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-running-windows-95: Windows 95 OSR 2.5 running on an Amstrad Sega Mega PC? Yes, slowly! A 4 GB Disk on Module, Netscape 4.8 and old-school gaming make for a memorable experiment. 🖥️
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-athlon-500mhz-rebu: An Amstrad Mega PC gets another rethink while a treasured Slot A Athlon 500 MHz system returns to life. There's also a tiny picoPSU and lots of storage drama. 💾
/new-camera-canon-eos-600d/: A Canon EOS 600D DSLR is on order to improve the blog's hardware photos. Meanwhile, the search for matching Amstrad Mega PC accessories continues. 📷
/sega-saturn-external-psu-dc-dc-converte: Three DC-DC converters arrive for the Sega Saturn external PSU project. An LED lights up in the first bench test, but proper voltage and load checks come next. 🔌
/new-purchases-28-april-2012/: A Sega TeraDrive Model 2 is on its way from Japan, with a Genesis Nomad still inbound from the US. A new Canon EOS 600D is ready for hardware photos. 🖥️
/faulty-ethernet-card/: A sub-$3 ethernet card proves that even an RJ45 socket can go spectacularly wrong. The cable won't click in, the contacts look corroded, and it passed quality control. 🔌
/game-gear-capacitor-backlight-repair-an: Two Game Gears, two very different repair stories: one recapped and back to life, the other rescued from bad soldering with audio restored but power problems remaining. 🔧
/led-clock-counter-module-and-sega-terad: An LED counter races along at 50 Hz using a hacked Mega Drive controller, while a Sega TeraDrive Model 2 finally arrives from Japan. One excellent day for unusual hardware. 💡
/sega-mega-cd-karaoke-accessory-and-yuka: The Sega Mega-CD Karaoke box arrives with a dead microphone and an annoying buzz. A replacement cartridge is on order, alongside a boxed Yukawa Dreamcast from Japan. 🎤
/humble-beginnings-nintendo-famicom-inco: A boxed Japanese Famicom and a couple of games are on the way. The next challenge is a composite AV mod to bypass its RF output, with no guarantees and plenty to learn. 🎮
/sega-teradrive-model-2-genesis-nomad-an: A working TeraDrive runs Scorched Earth, a Genesis Nomad refuses to power on, and a seller sends the wrong Mega Drive. Three Sega machines, no shortage of tinkering. 🎮
/sega-teradrive-demo-sonic-1-and-sega-me: Sonic runs at 60 Hz on the Japanese Sega TeraDrive, while its built-in menu lets a Mega Drive controller launch DOS programs. The PC and console sides make an odd couple. 🎮
/sega-mega-cd-karaoke-microphone-faulty/: A temporary microphone brings a Sega Mega-CD Karaoke box back into the conversation, confirming the original capsule is faulty. The real replacement is still on its way. 🎤
/sega-teradrive-286-diagnostics/: Diagnostics on a Sega TeraDrive Model 2 reveal PC DOS 3.30, a curious RAM disk, 1991 component dates and a Western Digital video controller. Even its BIOS has mysteries. 💾
/sega-teradrive-with-windows-21-windows-: Windows 2.1 and 3.00a squeeze onto floppies for the 286-powered Sega TeraDrive, with a RAM disk speeding up Solitaire. A classic Game Boy joins the collection too. 💾
/japanese-sega-saturn-va0-dreamcast-and-: A white Japanese Saturn powers on but its CD mechanism clicks ominously, while an early VA0 Dreamcast arrives in lovely condition. The TeraDrive's power rails get checked too. 🔧
/sega-mega-cd-karaoke-microphone-repaire: A $10 BG-58 cartridge brings a faulty Sega Mega-CD Karaoke microphone back to life. Two solder joints, a slightly awkward fit and one accessory ready to sing again. 🎤
/faulty-japanese-sega-saturn-cd-drive-pr: A white Japanese Saturn's CD drive spins, clicks and shudders in alarming ways. Is the disc really turning backwards? Diagnosis is still ahead, and the noises aren't encouraging. 💿
/sega-genesis-nomad-dc-in-jack-repair/: A broken Genesis Nomad comes back to life after its shorting DC-in jack is replaced with one borrowed from a Mega Drive 2. New screen, clean buttons, actual handheld gaming. 🎮
/sega-teradrive-model-2-with-windows-311: Windows 3.11 boots from a floppy and RAM disk on a 286-powered Sega TeraDrive Model 2. It works, but with 2.5 MB of RAM, Solitaire isn't in any particular hurry. 💾
/the-sega-teradrive-model-3/: A Sega TeraDrive Model 3 arrives without its 30 MB hard drive. Windows runs from floppy, but finding a compatible replacement for that unusual 44-pin interface is another matter. 💾
/nintendo-famicom-composite-av-mod/: Three revisions turn a tangle of wires into a compact composite AV board for a Nintendo Famicom. Picture and sound work, although the infamous jailbars remain. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-with-picopsu-and-a: A tiny picoPSU powers an Amstrad Mega PC mainboard on the lounge-room floor, while a dual-screen Sega Saturn setup gets a workout. Keyboard problems still block proper testing. 🖥️
/long-weekends-and-nintendo-famicoms/: A Famicom AV mod is working, though jailbars remain. Add a haul of Japanese Saturn accessories, stubborn TeraDrive storage experiments and one deeply unwise PSU encounter. 🔧
/sega-teradrive-model-3-hard-drive-repla: Three IBM WDL-330P hard drives pass testing in a Sega TeraDrive Model 3, with DOS 6.22 and Windows 3.11 installed. One other drive sounds like a freight train. 💾
/sega-teradrive-model-2-and-model-3-stor: The TeraDrive Model 3 is happily running Windows from a 30 MB hard drive, while a Promise controller on the Model 2 detects a drive but still can't boot it. Close, but not quite. 💾
/sega-teradrive-puzzle-construction/: Sega's Puzzle Construction on the TeraDrive mixes PC software with Mega Drive graphics, music and controller input. Its sound editor is a strange and delightful bonus. 🎵
/286-386sx-and-486slc-overclocking-and-u: Socketed CPUs, switchable clock oscillators and faster 286, 386SX and 486SLC chips are on the drawing board. These are upgrade ideas, not finished overclocks. 🔧
/nintendo-famicom-av-mod-complete/: A Nintendo Famicom now has working composite video and audio thanks to a compact homemade board. The jailbars survived the repair, but Spelunker is ready for another go. 🎮
/faulty-voltron-t-500s-voltage-converter: A Voltron T-500S voltage converter arrives with a dodgy switch, worrying buzz, fake ventilation slots and a spelling mistake. Mains-powered quality control at its finest. 🔌
/sega-teradrive-hard-drive-interface-inv: The Sega TeraDrive's 44-pin hard-drive connector isn't ordinary IDE. A deep dive into IBM PS/2 storage reveals working WDL-330P drives and plenty of unanswered questions. 💾
/sega-mega-drive-frenzy/: Seven Mega Drives get opened for a photo session. A Thailand-built Model 1 hides a Hitachi CPU, different screws and a reminder that Sega hardware varies more than it looks. 🖥️
/chronix-nixie-clock-slot-machine-demo/: A Chronix Nixie clock puts on a glowing slot-machine display to keep its cathodes exercised. The spinning digits are a surprisingly entertaining bit of tube maintenance. ⏰
/learning-to-desolder-ics/: Practising IC removal on a scrap RAM board leads to liberated chips, a sulking heat gun and a few hard-earned lessons before tackling an Amstrad Mega PC processor. 🔧
/sega-saturn-cd-deck-diagnosis-ba6798s-s: A Japanese Sega Saturn's runaway CD mechanism puts the ROHM BA6798S motor driver under suspicion. It's a plausible lead, not a confirmed fix, so the search continues. 🔧
/sega-mega-drive-arcade-power-sticks-and: Two Mega Drive Arcade Power Sticks get a clean, while a Model 1 develops a green screen and rolling lines. Removing its shielding makes the fault vanish. Mystery unsolved. 🎮
/sega-mega-drive-32x-photos/: A boxed Sega 32X gets a photographic tour, from its curious AV connections to a towering Mega Drive and Mega-CD stack. There's even a Neptune-style mod on the wish list. 🎮
/sega-mega-drive-2-dc-in-power-socket-re: A Mega Drive 2 loses power whenever its cable moves. The culprit is a cracked DC-in solder joint, and a quick reflow gets the console reliably running again. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-386sx-cpu-replacem: The Amstrad Mega PC's AMD 386SX is earmarked for removal in a bold TI486SXLC2 upgrade experiment. Clock rates, voltage requirements and a heat gun complicate the plan. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-486sxlc-cpu-upgrad: A 386SX comes off an Amstrad Mega PC and a TI486SXLC2 goes in, but the board won't boot. Plenty learnt about QFP soldering, at a rather expensive hardware cost. 💥
/sega-saturn-sophia-development-kit-inte: A Sega Saturn Sophia development kit gets an internal tour, revealing stacked boards, vintage chips and missing SH-2 processor cards. Cleaning comes first; testing must wait. 🖥️
/geist-force-prototype-reproduction-for-: An unfinished Geist Force prototype gets a limited Dreamcast reproduction through the ASSEMblergames community. Preservation wins, even if the game was never completed. 🎮
/sega-mega-drive-video-flicker-and-the-s: A Mega Drive's yellow and green video flicker disappears after warming up. The Sony CXA1145P encoder looks suspicious, and a later replacement confirms the diagnosis. 🔧
/hibernation-mode-activated/: House-moving and winter weather put the retro projects on a slower setting. Parts are still arriving, and a troublesome Mega Drive gets its LED and volume slider repaired. 🖥️
/acquisitions-inbound-pal-va0-dreamcast-: An unusual PAL VA0 Dreamcast bears a display-only warning, while an Accolade development cart and Macintosh LC 475 join the queue. There's a Neptune-style 32X plan too. 🎮
/mega-cd-bios-loading-for-the-amstrad-me: A Mega EverDrive can load Mega-CD BIOS software for an Amstrad Mega PC or Sega TeraDrive experiment. Making the physical expansion connection work is another challenge. 💾
/sega-saturn-rolling-horizontal-lines-ps: Rolling lines on PAL Sega Saturns mysteriously vanish when fed the wrong mains voltage. An accidental undervoltage test offers a clue, absolutely not a repair method. ⚡
/photographing-the-sega-saturn-collectio: A photo session with early VA0 Saturns reveals striking similarities between their SH-1 CD boards and those inside the Sophia development kit. Compatibility is untested. 📷
/sega-saturn-va0-lid-repair-and-sega-ral: A replacement CD lid gets an early VA0 Sega Saturn detecting discs again. The hardware behaves beautifully during Sega Rally, even if the driving is considerably less polished. 🏁
/sega-saturn-laser-assembly-replacement/: A donor laser from a faulty Japanese Saturn rescues a PAL machine that wouldn't read discs. The optical pickup swap finally delivers a working drive and a welcome repair win. 🔧
/sega-mega-drive-32x-jittery-video-initi: Three used Sega 32X units develop strange video issues, including Doom graphics that jitter after warm-up. A later Sega service bulletin points towards Mega Drive VA4 timing. 🎮
/sega-mega-drive-32x-repair-no-display-n: A Sega 32X that showed no picture or sound responds to a clean-up of its internal ribbon connections. Doom finally appears, while three other units still need answers. 🔧
/sega-mega-drive-model-1-cxa1145p-video-: Replacing the Sony CXA1145P video encoder cures a Mega Drive's yellow and green flicker. The soldering gets messy, but Knuckles is finally out of disco mode. 🎮
/sega-saturn-pal-power-supply-voltage-me: A faulty PAL Sega Saturn still refuses to start, even though its PSU measures roughly 3.36 V, 9.25 V and 5 V. Decent readings, but not yet a diagnosis. 🔧
/sega-saturn-ba6798s-motor-driver-replac: A five-dollar BA6798S motor driver goes into a deranged Sega Saturn CD deck. The soldering succeeds, but the drive is still completely berserk. Pizza cancelled. 🔧
/sega-mega-cd-ii-with-a-region-modded-me: Region switches on a Mega Drive II get a workout with the Mega-CD II. Changing to 60 Hz gets things moving, although the audio and video timing still have surprises. 🎮
/the-apple-macintosh-lc-475/: An Apple Macintosh LC 475 gets a fresh system and some classic games. The pizza-box Mac works, despite a damaged case, rust and a hard drive making horrible noises. 🍎
/the-ibm-ps2-model-30-8086-external-over: An Australian-made IBM PS/2 Model 30 brings an 8 MHz 8086, Sound Blaster audio and a hard drive full of bad sectors. Prince of Persia still gets a workout. 💾
/ibm-ps2-model-30-8086-disassembly/: An hour-long IBM PS/2 Model 30 teardown reveals unusual storage connections, a battered hard drive and plenty of 1987 engineering. Floppy booting survives the rebuild. 🔧
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-ram-utilisation-: System 7 makes a 36 MB Macintosh LC 475 look absurdly hungry for RAM. Switching from 24-bit to 32-bit addressing makes the missing memory properly usable. 🍎
/geist-force-prototype-reproduction-arri: The unreleased Dreamcast game Geist Force finally arrives as a beautiful community reproduction. The postman has mangled the packaging, but the prototype lives on. 🎮
/sega-mega-cd-ii-fuse-repair-and-sol-fea: A dead Mega-CD II gets a proper replacement for its blown F301 fuse. Batman Returns and Sonic CD run again, with a little Sol-Feace gameplay to celebrate. 🔧
/space-harrier-for-the-sega-mega-drive-3: Space Harrier on the Sega 32X brings colourful sprites, scaling effects and arcade chaos. For once the add-on is being used for games instead of endless repairs. 🎮
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-system-setup-dem: An LC 475 gets System 7.5.3, floppy transfers and a few beloved old games. Its hard drive sounds dreadful, but this Macintosh has finally become usable again. 🍎
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-and-mega-drive-32x: Two rare Aiwa Mega-CD CSD-GM1 machines arrive with problems, including cracked circuit boards and bad audio. Meanwhile the 32X video mystery points towards the host Mega Drive. 🔧
/amstrad-ppc640d-internal-view-relative-: An Amstrad PPC640D gets opened up for a look at its twin boards, floppy mechanism and removable modem. Under the lid lurks an 8 MHz 8086 and 640 KB of RAM. 💻
/creative-labs-cd-200-2x-cd-rom-driver-h: The Creative Labs CD-200 plays music but refuses to read data under DOS. Its deceptively IDE-like Panasonic interface sends the driver hunt into another round. 💿
/ibm-ps2-model-30-8086-720k-floppy-drive: A $10 replacement floppy drive for an IBM PS/2 Model 30 costs around $60 to ship. It looks compatible, but DOS won't boot and the machine keeps dropping into BASIC. 💾
/sharp-pc-4521-internal-view/: A Sharp PC-4521 portable gets an internal tour, revealing a NEC V40, an unusually wide LCD and a stubborn JVC hard drive. Not mine, but too interesting to ignore. 💻
/creative-labs-cd-200-2x-cd-rom-driver-s: Success! The Creative Labs CD-200 finally reads discs under DOS using CCD.SYS and MSCDEX. Removing one troublesome jumper helps end the driver nightmare. 💿
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-initial-damag: One Aiwa CSD-GM1 works poorly; the other has enormous cracks, broken traces and a missing chunk of PCB. Restoring power is only the beginning of this rescue. 🔧
/osborne-australia-486dx2-66-overview/: An Australian-made Osborne 486DX2-66 brings back childhood memories, with 64 MB RAM, a Sound Blaster Pro 2 and an enormous beige case. The CD-ROM finally works too. 💻
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-repairs-inter: One smashed Aiwa Mega-CD regains power and runs Mega Turrican with borrowed parts. The CD and audio faults remain, and now its supposedly good twin has stopped working. 🔧
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-repairs-part-: Jumper wires bring an Aiwa CSD-GM1 mainboard back to life, and a borrowed CD mechanism reaches the Sega startup screen. Video works, but audio and CD still need help. 🎮
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-external-power-sup: An external 12 V supply wakes the Aiwa CSD-GM1's radio and tape sections, but the Mega Drive hardware stays silent. There's more power-rail detective work ahead. ⚡
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-repairing-the-crac: Cracked traces on an Aiwa CSD-GM1 mainboard get bridged with colourful wires. After plenty of continuity checks, the red power light returns. One victory, many faults left. 🔧
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-where-has-all-the-: Where has all the bass gone? An Aiwa Mega-CD sounds thin and tinny, with a mysterious hum on bright screens. The audio fault remains an unsolved puzzle. 🎵
/wyse-technology-wy2112-40-286-overview/: A gigantic Wyse 2112-40 houses a 12.5 MHz 286, eight slots and a hefty Seagate hard drive. It won't boot properly yet, but there's plenty of hardware to explore. 💻
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-repairs-part-2-pow: The Aiwa Mega-CD's power rails get traced through transformer wiring and DC-DC converters. The game side is only seeing about 3.3 V, and the video looks awful. ⚡
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-more-power-problem: A rotten cold interrupts the Aiwa Mega-CD repairs, but the to-do list keeps growing: power regulators, distorted video, missing audio and temperamental CD drives. 🤧
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-wavy-video-and-pow: An Aiwa Mega-CD develops wavy video when powered by an external supply. The picture cleans up with the original transformer, leaving another electrical mystery to solve. 📺
/inside-the-aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-game-un: The detachable Aiwa CSD-GM1 Game Unit isn't quite a useless frisbee. Its Mega Drive section can run independently, but the Mega-CD still needs the stereo's CD mechanism. 🎮
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-kss-210b-lase: A new KSS-210B optical pickup lets an Aiwa Mega-CD recognise all 13 tracks on a disc. Playback still skips, but at least the laser replacement made real progress. 💿
/osborne-486-525-inch-floppy-drive-addit: A 5.25-inch floppy drive from a Wyse 286 boots the Osborne 486 beautifully. An LC 475 ethernet card also joins the growing pile of useful retro parts. 💾
/osborne-486-boot-sector-virus-cleanup-w: The Osborne 486 has a boot-sector visitor: F-PROT detects ABCD.A in the MBR. Infected floppies complicate the story, but the cleanup tool gives this old PC a chance. 🦠
/osborne-486-windows-95-installation-dem: Windows 95 finally starts on the Osborne 486, complete with sound and a very fussy Creative CD-ROM. Some CD-Rs work, others freeze it. Vintage computing bliss. 💻
/ibm-ps2-model-30-8086-sound-video-and-c: An IBM PS/2 Model 30 gets an NEC V30, 8087 maths coprocessor, VGA and Sound Blaster upgrades. Monkey Island is rather happier on the improved 8 MHz machine. 💾
/sega-dreamcast-pal-revision-va0/: A rare PAL VA0 Dreamcast has an April 1999 shell date and a display-only warning label. It may be a pre-launch unit, but its original purpose remains unproven. 🎮
/sega-dreamcast-pal-va0-internal-update/: Inside a rare PAL VA0 Dreamcast, the motherboard markings confirm the early revision. Its heatpipe hardware and unusual connectors invite more questions than answers. 🔧
/collection-overview-28th-october-2012/: Two bookcases, two TeraDrives and a frankly unreasonable amount of Sega hardware. An October 2012 collection tour proves that the real upgrade needed is more shelving. 🎮
/leaking-nicad-batteries-and-motherboard: Leaking NiCad barrel batteries leave ugly corrosion on two vintage 486 motherboards. The cells come out, and both boards still show signs of life. Not bad! 🔧
/sega-dreamcast-translucent-grey-shell-r: A yellowed Dreamcast gets a translucent smokey-grey replacement shell. The original case is preserved, and the rebuild even survives a collapsing camera tripod. 🎮
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-game-unit-overview: Two Aiwa Mega-CD Game Units reveal different capacitor colours and a rechargeable VL2020 backup battery. A recap is planned, but the audio mystery persists. 🔧
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-boot-failure-dom-a: An Amstrad Mega PC misbehaves with a Disk on Module, then boots normally from its original 107 MB hard drive. The exact DOM fault remains a mystery. 💾
/sega-dreamcast-bios-dumping-guide/: A Dreamcast Broadband Adapter and httpd-ack retrieve a PAL MPR-21871 BIOS dump over the network. The CRC32 matches revision 1.01c. Preservation achieved! 💾
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-startup-scree: What is the Japanese Aiwa Mega-CD startup screen saying? A community translation reveals prompts to press Start, check the disc and wait a little bit. Finally! 🎮
/picopsu-80-on-a-pentium-iii-800mhz/: A picoPSU-80 runs a Pentium III 800 MHz computer at about 37 to 38 W from the wall. Promising numbers, though a proper full-load test is still needed. ⚡
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-derating-tantalu: Planning a Macintosh LC 475 recap means thinking about tantalum capacitor voltage derating, package sizes and reliability. No capacitors replaced just yet. 🔧
/sega-saturn-model-1-va0-modchip-install: An early PAL VA0 Sega Saturn gets a 20-pin-compatible modchip, careful insulation and a successful test with Radiant Silvergun and Guardian Heroes. 🎮
/sega-teradrive-bios-dump-and-isa-memory: A Sega TeraDrive PC BIOS gets preserved with DOS DEBUG. Another owner's 6.5 MB RAM setup sparks ideas about ISA memory cards and future RAM-disk experiments. 💾
/sega-mega-cd-karaoke-unit-and-cdg-demo/: The repaired Mega-CD karaoke microphone gets another workout with CD+G graphics, echo effects and questionable singing. Four power adapters required. 🎤
/sega-mega-drive-32x-distorted-video-par: A 32X flicker mystery prompts experiments with grounding plates and Mega-CD video. Later Sega bulletins point to VA4 Mega Drive timing faults instead. 🔧
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-mismatched-vram-: Mixing 256 KB and 512 KB VRAM SIMMs makes an LC 475 display go spectacularly wrong. A replacement power supply works nicely, at least. Science achieved. 🍎
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-activating-pc-only: A jumper forces an Amstrad Mega PC into PC-only mode without its Mega Drive ISA card, making RAM tests on a 486SLC replacement board rather easier. 💻
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-adlib-sound-repair: An Amstrad Mega PC has missing or distorted AdLib sound. The problem isn't a missing DOS driver, so the investigation turns to the Sega card's connections and alignment. 🔊
/amstrad-sega-mega-pc-hard-drive-capacit: A tantalum capacitor on the Mega PC's 107 MB Seagate drive goes up in smoke. A replacement disk gets DOS and Windows for Workgroups 3.11 running again. 💥
/gravis-ultrasound-max-rev-18-demo/: The Gravis UltraSound MAX Rev 1.8 gets a MIDI demonstration, complete with sample-based sound and the occasional crackle. It's enormous, and there's more to learn. 🎵
/gq-4x-eeprom-and-eprom-programmer-test/: A USB GQ-4X programmer starts reading modem ROMs and the Amstrad Mega PC BIOS. A useful addition for future EPROM experiments, despite one missing adapter. 💾
/ibm-ps2-model-30-8086-with-isa-xtide-ca: An IBM PS/2 Model 30 recognises an ISA XTIDE controller and a wildly oversized 4 GB Disk on Module. DOS can access the storage, after some partitioning adventures. 💾
/miscellaneous-isa-and-pci-cards/: Gravis UltraSound, Sound Blaster, 3dfx, SCSI, modems and enough ISA and PCI cards to furnish a museum. Now to find enough working PCs to install them in. 🖥️
/mitsumi-newtronics-a-floppy-drive-that-: A Mitsumi Newtronics 5.25-inch drive briefly springs to life after fixing a bad edge-connector contact, then starts reporting track-zero errors again. Almost! 💾
/nec-fd1157c-cleaning-a-troublesome-flop: Cleaning the heads of an NEC FD1157C 1.2 MB floppy drive reveals a filthy mechanism, but the drive still refuses to read disks. No miracle repair today. 🔧
/recovering-from-an-incorrect-xtide-eepr: One incorrect XTIDE EEPROM flash stops a Disk on Module being detected. A GQ-4X and a known-good chip recover the firmware, but storage still needs work. 💾
/sega-teradrive-model-2-installing-windo: Windows 3.1 finally installs on a 10 MHz Sega TeraDrive Model 2, using XTIDE and a 2 GB Disk on Module instead of a heroic collection of floppy disks. 🪟
/sega-teradrive-model-2-with-xtide-card-: A quick demonstration of the Sega TeraDrive Model 2 booting through XTIDE to a Disk on Module, with a 286, 2.5 MB RAM and rather more storage than Sega intended. 💾
/sega-teradrive-model-2-xtide-boot-succe: Victory for the Sega TeraDrive Model 2: repartitioning a Disk on Module and rebuilding the MBR finally lets XTIDE boot straight into MS-DOS 6.22. 💾
/sega-teradrive-model-3-with-xtide-insta: Both the original 30 MB hard drive and XTIDE storage boot in a TeraDrive Model 3. Even better, its Model 2 sibling now has working modern storage too. 💾
/xtide-settings-for-the-sega-teradrive/: XTIDE BIOS settings for the Sega TeraDrive get documented, from controller options to the boot menu. Hopefully that saves a future evening of firmware archaeology. 💾
/nec-fd1157c-more-floppy-drive-fault-fin: An NEC FD1157C floppy drive sometimes reads disks when pressure is applied to its head, then returns to errors. A clue, perhaps, but certainly not a repair. 💾
/wyse-2112-40-286-revival-project/: A Wyse 2112-40 286 escapes the parts pile and boots DOS again. Its hard drive, keyboard and speed-switching features are working, with Paku Paku as the reward. 🖥️
/the-amstrad-ppc640d-portable-8086-overv: An accidental eBay bid brings home an Amstrad PPC640D with dual 720 KB floppy drives, an 8 MHz 8086 and a display with truly dreadful viewing angles. 💻
/unichip-486-wb-4407-rev-11-motherboard-: A donated Unichip 486 motherboard arrives with a DX2-66, three VLB slots and its NiCad battery already removed. It looks promising, but hasn't been power-tested. 🖥️
/christmas-special-2012-spam-attack/: Christmas Day brings a very questionable bacon-flavoured SPAM taste test instead of vintage hardware repairs. The verdict? Please bring back the computers. 🎄
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-solid-state-scsi: A PCD-60B SCSI card reader and CompactFlash card give the Macintosh LC 475 silent solid-state boot storage. A far nicer alternative to its noisy old hard drive. 🍎
/console-collection-overview-28th-decemb: The Sega collection gets rearranged into side-by-side shelves for a final 2012 tour. Somehow there are seven Mega Drive 2s and even less room to move. 🎮
/sega-mega-drive-2-dc-in-socket-repair-a: A Mega Drive 2 gets its cracked DC-in solder joint repaired, only to reveal strange video, white screens and resets. One fix uncovers another problem. 🔧
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-removing-the-soc: Removing the socketed 68LC040 from a Macintosh LC 475 makes way for a full 68040 experiment. Careful levering beats bent pins, and cooling needs attention too. 🍎
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-overclocking-to-: Two tiny resistor moves take an LC 475 from 25 MHz to 33 MHz. The Macintosh boots and benchmarks improve, although a replacement 68040's FPU remains a puzzle. 🍎
/queen-sugar-ant-revenge-of-the-ant-quee: An enormous sugar ant turns up indoors and might be a queen. It's certainly got an attitude! Identification remains uncertain, but it's going back outside. 🐜
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-4-gb-hitachi-mic: Two 4 GB Hitachi Microdrives refuse to cooperate with an LC 475's SCSI card reader. CompactFlash works, so the investigation moves to formatting and drive geometry. 💾
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-online-with-pds-: A PDS ethernet card puts the Macintosh LC 475 online with Mac OS 7.6.1. Netscape loads the old website, slowly, and YouTube is understandably a bit much. 🌐
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-slowing-the-fan-: A resistor makes the LC 475's extra cooling fan quieter, though some values stop it starting at all. The wiring works, but airflow and clearance still matter. 🔧
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-tantalum-capacit: Leaking capacitors on an LC 475 logic board get replaced with tantalums. The soldering is educational, but the Macintosh boots and the sound still works. 🍎
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-modifications-ov: After weeks of tinkering, the LC 475 has 33 MHz speed, 36 MB RAM, 1 MB VRAM, CompactFlash storage, ethernet and new capacitors. Not so stock anymore. 🍎
/my-fifteen-minutes-starts-now/: A chat with MasterControl90 becomes an Italian-language interview about Sega, retro computers and gaming memories. My fifteen minutes of fame have arrived! 🎮
/hackintosh-rebuild-asrock-775dual-915gl: An ASRock 775Dual-915GL motherboard returns for a Hackintosh nostalgia rebuild, complete with a cheap case, Celeron-era memories and a pile of old PC parts. 🖥️
/sega-saturn-sophia-and-va0-parts-compat: Can Sega Saturn Sophia development-kit CD hardware run in a retail VA0 Saturn? A mechanism swap and laser adjustment produce promising results, with caveats. 🔧
/sega-teradrive-scanliner-demo-with-15kh: A VGA scanline generator gives the Sega TeraDrive's 15 kHz Mega Drive RGB output an old-school CRT look. Sonic & Knuckles has never looked so good. 🎮
/stone-age-gamer-deluxe-mega-everdrive-s: A Deluxe Mega EverDrive arrives from Stone Age Gamer, beautifully packaged and numbered 123. Only problem: there's no Mega Drive handy to test it! 🎁
/wyse-2112-40-286-final-overview/: The enormous Wyse 2112-40 finally has working floppy drives, a 40 MB hard drive and DOS. One last tour before this rescued 286 heads to a new home. 💾
/36v-lithium-battery-corrosion-damage/: A leaking 3.6 V lithium battery has spread corrosion across somebody else's Macintosh LC 475 motherboard. A nasty reminder to inspect old PRAM cells. 🔋
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-256-mb-pcmcia-fl: A 256 MB PCMCIA flash card gets a more encouraging workout in the LC 475's PCD-60B SCSI reader, while SD cards and Microdrives continue to resist. 💾
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-revenge-of-the-m: The Hitachi Microdrives return for more Macintosh LC 475 formatting experiments. Mac OS X, disk images and stubborn partitions still can't make them work. 💾
/drilling-region-switch-holes-in-a-sega-: Two Mega Drive 2 region mods need neatly drilled switch holes. A damaged shell becomes the practice target, with sock puppetry and video interference thrown in. 🔧
/vl400c-i-486-motherboard-failure/: A VL400C-I 486 board briefly looks promising after changing a Gate A20 jumper, then starts losing extended memory again. Another motherboard for the scrap pile. 💻
/removing-an-eprom-from-a-sega-prototype: Removing one EPROM from a four-chip Sega Monopoly cartridge doesn't stop it booting, but gameplay gets wonderfully weird. An unusual little experiment. 🎮
/sega-mega-drive-2-50hz-60hz-mod-mark-ii: A second attempt at a Mega Drive 2 region mod brings tidy toggle switches and working 50 Hz / 60 Hz selection, without the previous console's blue rolling lines. 🎮
/sega-mega-drive-32x-jittery-video-va4-s: The jittery Sega 32X picture isn't necessarily a faulty add-on. Sega's service bulletins point to unstable EDCLK and VCLK signals on affected Mega Drive VA4 boards. 🔧
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-bios-dump-mpr-1576: An Aiwa CSD-GM1 BIOS ROM gets removed and dumped for preservation. The elusive MPR-15768-T finally has a digital backup, after some adventurous desoldering. 💾
/cross-products-snasm-mega-cd-developmen: A rare Cross Products SNASM Mega-CD development unit joins the collection, complete with extra connectors, switches and PC development hardware to investigate. 🖥️
/hanzo-sega-dreamcast-vga-box-and-scanli: The HANZO VGA box gives a Dreamcast crisp video and adjustable scanlines, with enough switches to cause confusion. Sonic Adventure 2 provides the test. 🎮
/tefal-actifry-potato-chip-cooker-demons: A Tefal ActiFry turns four potatoes into decent chips with a spoonful of oil. The timer sounds dreadful, but dinner on an A4 sheet of paper is a success. 🍟
/sophia-systems-sega-saturn-programming-: Months of cleaning and nearly 300 photographs bring the Sega Saturn Sophia devkit closer to reassembly. Missing SH-2 CPU boards remain the main obstacle. 🔧
/cross-products-snasm-mega-cd-developmen: A Cross Products SNASM Mega-CD development unit powers up for PC interface experiments. DOS utilities, huge ISA cards and power requirements still need sorting. 💾
/name-that-tune-the-mystery-tune-of-myst: An unidentified tune from an old recording gets a 50 Hz versus 60 Hz speed experiment. Keygen music, Amiga, Commodore 64? The mystery remains unsolved. 🎵
/cross-products-snasm-mega-cd-developmen: Inside a rare Cross Products SNASM Mega-CD development unit: modified Sega hardware, extra boards and a forest of connectors. Getting it apart is half the adventure. 🔧
/accolade-code-monkeys-dev-cart-for-the-: An Accolade development cartridge linked to The Code Monkeys boots an introduction on the Mega Drive, but its mysterious 9-pin cable still needs explaining. 🎮
/disk-on-modules-and-the-xtide-bios-on-t: Three Disk on Modules, three different headaches on a Sega TeraDrive. XTIDE recognises some, powers others, and reminds us that compatibility isn't guaranteed. 💾
/micomsoft-xrgb-mini-framemeister-arriva: The XRGB-mini Framemeister arrives, but the Japanese RGB21 adapter needs rewiring for EuroSCART. A little soldering delivers wonderfully crisp Mega Drive RGB over HDMI. 📺
/sega-teradrive-xtide-eeprom-upgrade-at2: Upgrading XTIDE EEPROMs from AT28C64B to AT28C256 gives the Sega TeraDrive cards four times the ROM space. A new BIOS build gets things moving again. 💾
/toaplans-zero-wing-demo-on-the-xrgb-min: Zero Wing on the Mega Drive looks glorious through the Framemeister's scanlines. Surviving past the first stage is another matter. All your base! 🎮
/sega-genesis-nomad-on-the-xrgb-mini-fra: A Sega Genesis Nomad looks beautiful through the XRGB-mini Framemeister, while the Mega Drive 2 refuses to display. Time to investigate the RGB sync wiring. 🎮
/roadside-pc-rescue-core-2-quad-q8400-an: A rain-soaked PC rescued from the roadside comes with a Core 2 Quad, Radeon HD 5770, cockroaches and a fleeing lizard. The original PSU goes straight in the bin. 🦎
/final-cut-pro-x-vs-imovie-908-vs-lizard: Final Cut Pro X isn't winning me over, iMovie 9.0.8 is buggy but familiar, and the surprise star is a lizard rescued from a roadside PC's power supply. 🎬
/roadside-core-2-quad-initial-test-and-d: A roadside Core 2 Quad survives its wet adventure, with onboard video and Radeon HD 5770 both working. The rescued computer gets donated to a Linux enthusiast. 🖥️
/southern-leaf-tailed-gecko-wizard-lizar: A southern leaf-tailed gecko pays another visit indoors and refuses to cooperate with the relocation box. Such a clever little wizard lizard. 🦎
/xrgb-mini-on-sega-mega-drive-2-without-: Removing an LM1881 sync stripper from a custom Mega Drive 2 RGB cable finally gets a stable picture on the Framemeister. This wiring doesn't need it. 📺
/sega-saturn-sophia-sh-2-cpu-cards-171-6: Two 171-6692B SH-2 CPU cards finally arrive for Sega's Sophia devkit. They're close to the expected D revision, but missing power headers and jumpers complicate things. 🔧
/accessing-the-sega-ibm-teradrive-built-: Need the Sega TeraDrive's built-in setup? Choose DOS, then press F1 during PC startup. Three humble settings, including a power-on beep, await your attention. 💾
/asus-eeebox-b202-disassembly-and-upgrad: An ASUS EeeBox B202 gets opened up to reach its wireless card and other components. Tiny Atom-era PC, enormous collection of screws and fragile clips. 🪛
/converting-xrgb-mini-adapter-to-eurosca: Japanese RGB21 and EuroSCART look identical but aren't wired alike. The Framemeister adapter gets traced with a multimeter and rewired for European RGB cables. 🔌
/mean-machines-sega-mega-cd-preview-vhs-: A 1992 Mean Machines Sega VHS previews the Mega-CD with Night Trap, Sewer Shark, Batman Returns and more. The tape survives, though the audio stutters. 📼
/vhs-sega-saturn-magazine-exclusive-vhs-: An exclusive VHS from the first Official Sega Saturn Magazine shows off Virtua Fighter 2, Sega Rally, Virtua Cop and more. A slice of 1995 Sega hype preserved. 📼
/good-capacitor-bulged-capacitor-visual-: Two 680 uF capacitors, one healthy and one bulging around its base. A useful visual comparison, with a reminder that failed capacitors don't always look damaged. 🔧
/hakko-808-desoldering-tool-removing-a-f: The Hakko 808 desoldering gun makes removing a dead through-hole capacitor almost enjoyable. Hot nozzle, vacuum pump and a far cleaner board afterwards. 🔧
/sega-saturn-sophia-a-bus-capacitor-repl: Sophia's A-Bus board gets six fresh 220 uF capacitors with help from a Hakko 808. The soldering goes well, but the Saturn devkit still refuses to boot. 🔧
/dreamshell-400-rc1-boot-attempt-with-sd: DreamShell 4.0.0 RC1 sometimes recognises an SD adapter, sometimes complains about the file system. No reliable Dreamcast game boot yet, and the outcome stays unresolved. 💾
/sega-saturn-sophia-programming-box-main: Replacing electrolytics on Sega's Sophia mainboard finally brings a video signal and a clock-setting screen. Progress at last, though plenty of repairs remain. 🔧
/nixie-clock-36v-nicad-battery-replaceme: A Chronix Nixie clock swaps its 3.6 V NiCad backup battery for a NiMH pack. The experiment works in this clock, but charging compatibility matters. ⏰
/apple-iic-internal-quick-look/: Inside a faulty Apple IIc: a tidy 65C02 computer, integrated floppy hardware and an unresolved power problem. A quick tour before the camera battery dies. 🍎
/australian-daddy-long-legs-spider-catch: An Australian daddy long legs spider catches its lunch. Also, a reminder that cellar spiders, harvestmen and crane flies shouldn't all be confused. 🕷️
/sausage-puppy-attacks/: Meet Pepper, a clever little sausage dog who already knows their name. Coco and Prinny make brief appearances, but this puppy steals the show. 🐶
/introducing-the-navir-super-optic-wonde: A childhood Navir Super Optic Wonder turns up with a torch, whistle, compass, sundial and binoculars. One leaked battery and half a monocular later, it still has charm. 🔦
/sega-saturn-model-2-modchip-installatio: A Japanese Model 2 Saturn gets a modchip configured for its 0014 CD board. A little soldering and insulation later, the test game actually boots. 🎮
/sophia-systems-sega-saturn-programming-: Sophia's capacitor restoration is finally complete after months of work. Fresh components across multiple boards help bring the Sega Saturn devkit back to life. 🔧
/phantasy-star-iv-on-the-xrgb-mini-frame: Phantasy Star IV looks gorgeous through the Framemeister on a Mega Drive 2. The RGB is sharp, even if navigating the academy is less successful. 🎮
/original-xbox-initial-damage-assessment: An original Xbox arrives with mystery wires, a taped-in 9 V battery, damaged controller ports and a leaking clock capacitor. What happened to this poor console? 🔧
/original-xbox-clock-capacitor-cleanup-a: A leaking clock capacitor gets cleaned up inside an original Xbox, along with other damaged components. The machine boots and plays Burnout Revenge again. 🎮
/sony-playstation-ps-one-internal-overvi: A Sony PS one gets opened up to revisit a modchip installed back in high school. The old soldering and spaghetti wiring have held up rather nicely. 🎮
/raspberry-pi-berryboot-raspbian-wheezy-: BerryBoot and Raspbian Wheezy get a Raspberry Pi running, with plans for FTP, remote access and a retro file server. The server jobs are still ahead. 🥧
/bosch-phg-630-dce-heat-gun-destructive-: A Bosch heat gun gets tested on an already-dead Xbox motherboard, lifting the CPU in a decidedly destructive experiment. Salvage, not a proper repair. 🔥
/original-xbox-softmod-to-tsop-flash-pro: An original Xbox TSOP flash attempt goes wrong, leaving the softmod broken and Error 21 on screen. Fortunately, the hard drive and EEPROM were backed up. 🎮
/xbox-original-softmod-recovery/: An Xbox dashboard disappears after a troubled softmod and TSOP experiment. Ndure and XboxHDM provide the tools for a recovery attempt, with backups proving vital. 💾
/xbox-original-tsop-flash-overview/: Damaged solder pads complicate an original Xbox Winbond TSOP flash, but a little jumper-wire repair leads to a successful Xecuter2 BIOS installation. 🎮
/23andme-dna-discovery-test-kit/: A 23andMe DNA kit gets unboxed, registered and prepared for its trip to the US. Saliva collection has never looked so glamorous. Results still to come. 🧬
/burnout-3-failing-to-load-on-tsop-flash: Burnout 3 refuses to start on a TSOP-flashed Xbox, while Burnout Revenge works. The eventual culprit isn't the console after all, but a bad game file. 🎮
/burnout-revenge-one-not-so-hot-lap/: Burnout Revenge delivers one not-so-hot lap and a silver medal. Shortcuts are a lie, apparently. Or perhaps the driving just needs a little work. 🏎️
/original-xbox-psu-cracked-ac-input-sold: An original Xbox power supply buzzes and arcs at the AC input. A cracked solder joint is repaired, stopping the arcing, but mains circuitry demands care. ⚡
/sega-saturn-sophia-171-6692b-sh-2-power: Sophia's 171-6692B SH-2 boards lack the usual power header. A custom cable adapts the 2.0 mm connectors so these unusual CPU cards can work. 🔌
/xrgb-mini-framemeister-remote-overlay/: The Framemeister's Japanese remote gets a labelled vinyl overlay courtesy of a forum member. Beautiful RGB pictures are nicer when you know what the buttons do. 📺
/wolfenstein-3d-on-sega-saturn-early-vbt: An early Wolfenstein 3D Saturn port runs in emulators but proves stubborn on Sophia and retail hardware. The real-console experiment remains unresolved. 🎮
/cheap-capacitor-tester-demonstration/: A cheap capacitor tester produces some convincing readings and some wildly suspicious ones. ESR and capacitance are useful, but this gadget may need testing itself. 🔧
/netgear-dg834gv5-modem-router-overheati: A Netgear DG834Gv5 router develops browned plastic, occasional crashes and weak Wi-Fi. Heatsinks look promising, but the cooling mod hasn't happened yet. 🌡️
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-checking-cpu-cap: A supposedly full 68040 in an LC 475 reports no FPU in TattleTech. The 33 MHz Mac still runs, but what exactly was inside that replacement CPU? 🍎
/seagate-st3120a-hard-drive-capacitor-re: The Amstrad Mega PC's smoky Seagate ST3120A gets two new tantalum capacitors. No fireworks this time, and the 107 MB drive boots DOS 5.0 again. 💾
/sega-saturn-sophia-simm-cart-dip-switch: Sega Saturn Sophia's SIMM CART DIP switch isn't a simple cartridge selector. It changes memory mapping, with side effects for external RAM cartridges. 🔧
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-8-gb-compactflas: An 8 GB CompactFlash card appears in the LC 475's PCD-60B SCSI reader, but formatting it is another story. Recognised doesn't mean ready to use! 🍎
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-hangman-plus-gam: Hangman Plus 2.0 returns on the Macintosh LC 475, complete with animal categories, dreadful guesses and far too much trouble identifying a turkey. 🎮
/apple-macintosh-lc-475-mac-os-standard-: An 8 GB CompactFlash card finally behaves in the LC 475 when split into roughly 2 GB Mac OS Standard partitions. Bigger partitions weren't cooperating. 💾
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-repair-status-june: Two Aiwa CSD-GM1 units, bad transformers, cracked boards and barely audible sound. June 2013 is a repair checkpoint, not a victory lap. 🔧
/apple-macbook-pro-geforce-8600m-gt-heat: A dead 17-inch MacBook Pro gets an uncontrolled heat-gun experiment around its GeForce 8600M GT. It boots again, but the result isn't a reliable repair method. 🔥
/xrgb-mini-framemeister-euroscart-adapte: Three XRGB-mini EuroSCART adapters get opened up and compared. One is messy, one is neatly built, and the DIY cable skips the troublesome sync stripper. 🔌
/inteldx4-overdrive-100mhz-486-workstati: A 100 MHz IntelDX4 OverDrive PC packs Sega Mega-CD development cards, Gravis UltraSound and 64 MB RAM. Expansion slots have officially become a contact sport. 🖥️
/sega-snasm2-and-cd-emulation-cards-with: SNASM2 Sega development cards are too enormous for one PC and fail their SCSI link test in another. A 486 starts looking like the sensible option. 💾
/snasm2-mega-cd-emulation-card-on-a-486d: Success at last! A 486DX4-100 with 64 MB RAM gets the SNASM2 Mega-CD development card communicating. Huge ISA cards, happy DOS workstation. 🎮
/doom-1666-gravis-ultrasound-vs-sound-bl: Doom 1.666 supplies the soundtrack as a Gravis UltraSound MAX battles a Sound Blaster 32. The music is lovely; finding room for both cards is not. 🎵
/black-mesa-quick-demo/: Black Mesa includes Office Space jokes and a beige PC that looks suspiciously like mine. Naturally I pick it up. That's my computer now, thanks! 🎮
/glitching-on-western-technologies-sega-: The Western Technologies Sega development card turns Sonic into a beautiful mess of corrupted graphics, strange music and occasional illegal instructions. 🎮
/isa-vlb-video-card-vram-mayhem-and-a-re: A one-dollar ISA video card resists every VRAM swap, while a more cooperative Trident card reaches 2 MB. The 486 workstation gets some useful rearranging. 🖥️
/snasm2-isa-card-on-a-pentium-class-moth: A Pentium motherboard finally passes SNASM2 tests when its internal CPU cache is disabled. Excellent for Sega development, dreadful for playing Doom. 💾
/western-technologies-sega-dev-card-demo: A Western Technologies Sega development kit includes example code and source files. The compiler isn't ready yet, but changing the demo text is on the wish list. 💻
SEGALOAD sends a Sonic binary from a DOS PC to SRAM on a Western Technologies Mega Drive development cart. Sonic actually runs! A rather satisfying test. 🎮
/western-technologies-sega-dev-card-sega: Converting Zero Wing from SMD to BIN lets SEGALOAD start it on a Sega development cartridge. It freezes later, but the software transfer works. 💾
/western-technologies-sega-dev-card-soft: SegaDev software talks to a Western Technologies Mega Drive development cartridge, exposing VRAM, CRAM, VSRAM and VDP registers. Programming comes later. 🎮
/faulty-damaged-super-nintendo-consoles-: Three faulty Super Nintendo consoles arrive on a dark, stormy night, each with a different combination of audio and video faults. Let the recapping begin. 🔧
/microsoft-xbox-360-initial-assessment-r: An Xbox 360 from 2008 shows the dreaded three red lights and no video. Dust, missing faceplate and a suspicious rattle greet the first inspection. 🎮
/sony-playstation-3-initial-assessment-y: A PlayStation 3 arrives with the Yellow Light of Death and absolutely no picture. Shims and other ideas can wait until the fault is understood. 🎮
/super-nintendo-serial-up15971140-video-: SNES UP15971140 has sound but its image is purple, flickering and sometimes backwards. Corrosion and leaking capacitors look suspicious, not yet conclusive. 📺
/super-nintendo-serial-up17388130-no-sou: SNES UP17388130 plays John Madden Football '93 with perfectly good video and absolutely no sound. First idea: replace the ageing capacitors. 🔧
/super-nintendo-serial-up17548016-no-vid: SNES UP17548016 powers up without video or sound, sporting a broken reset button and missing LED cover. The repair work is only beginning. 🎮
/super-nintendo-serial-up17548016-repair: A dead-looking SNES UP17548016 springs to life after a bent contact in its reset switch is repositioned. Video and sound return without a recap. 🔧
/sega-sophia-target-box-pal-switch-setti: PAL switch settings and SIMM details from my Sega Saturn Sophia Target Box, including an 8 MB module. These are observed settings, not universal factory defaults. 💾
/netgear-dg834gv5-adsl2-modem-router-coo: A fan, heatsinks and a little plastic surgery cool a toasty Netgear DG834Gv5. Running the fan around 9 V keeps the noise more civilised. 🌬️
/block-imaging-drives-with-dd-under-mac-: Using dd on Mac OS X to make raw disk images of classic Macintosh and Raspberry Pi media. Check the device number: copying the wrong way is not forgiving. 💾
/supercic-planning-notes-for-snsp-cpu-1c: SuperCIC sounds perfect for switchless region selection on a 1CHIP SNES, but the F413B lockout wiring differs from older guides. Still planning, not installed. 🎮
/xbox-360-rrod-repair-attempt-serial-072: An Xbox 360 RROD repair attempt involving X-clamps, screws and a heat gun ends in failure. The fast-forward footage is entertaining, at least. 🔧
/original-xbox-hitachi-lg-gdr-8050l-dvd-: An original Xbox Hitachi-LG DVD tray won't eject until a 25%-off sticker becomes an unlikely spacer in its magnetic clamp. Discount engineering works! 💿
/original-xbox-samsung-sdg-605-dvd-tray-: A stubborn Samsung SDG-605 Xbox DVD tray gets a discount-sticker spacer, while a drive-board swap rescues another mechanism. One working drive from two. 💿
/sony-playstation-3-ylod-repair-attempt/: A PlayStation 3 YLOD repair attempt involving heat, shims and enough thermal paste to decorate the bench ends without success. Diagnosis still needed. 🔧
/super-nintendo-dual-capacitor-replaceme: Two Super Nintendo motherboards get their electrolytics replaced at twenty times normal video speed. One lifted pad is repaired, but the original faults remain. 🔧
/super-nintendo-serial-up15971140-ppu1-t: Three corrosion-damaged traces around a Super Nintendo's PPU1 get bridged with wire. The bizarre graphics steadily improve until the picture looks normal. 🎮
/super-nintendo-serial-up17388130-no-sou: SNES UP17388130 remains silent after a recap. A closer look reveals a hole blown through its S-MIX chip, moving the audio investigation somewhere new. 🔧
/super-nintendo-serial-up17548016-capaci: A previously repaired SNES UP17548016 gets a maintenance recap using radial electrolytics. The reset switch, not the capacitors, fixed its original fault. 🔧
/tips-on-removing-smd-electrolytic-capac: Removing old SMD electrolytics by rocking them loose can lift pads, especially on corroded boards. This old workshop method deserves a clear warning. ⚠️
/damaged-s-mix-on-a-snes-snsp-cpu-1chip-: The SNES S-MIX audio chip has a hole in it. An LM324 substitution doesn't work, but bypassing the mixer produces some sound. Not a full repair. 🎵
/aiwa-mega-cd-game-unit-bios-socket-inst: An Aiwa Mega-CD Game Unit gets a proper BIOS socket and carefully bridged damaged traces. Continuity checks pass; the larger repair saga continues. 🔧
/aiwa-mega-cd-game-unit-bios-socket-prep: Removing the Aiwa Mega-CD BIOS for preservation left damaged connections behind. Socket preparation begins with a multimeter, trace maps and cautious optimism. 💾
/broken-damaged-sony-playstations-first-: A bargain pile of faulty original PlayStations brings broken lids, missing lasers, liquid damage and mystery modchips. At least donor parts are plentiful. 🎮
/sega-teradrive-ibm-wdl-330p-30mb-hard-d: Three IBM WDL-330P 30 MB drives offer a rare look at the TeraDrive's unusual storage hardware. There's a 1991 mechanism and plenty of capacitors to inspect. 💾
/sega-teradrive-wdl-330p-hard-drive-capa: Leaky capacitors get replaced on a Sega TeraDrive WDL-330P drive, with a lifted pad rescued by a small wire. Existing bad blocks remain, sadly. 🔧
/x0xb0x-10-adafruit-edition-quick-peek/: SuperNick's x0xb0x analogue synthesiser is still being assembled, but the Adafruit-era board looks wonderful. No finished music machine just yet. 🎵
/basic-testing-of-a-7806-voltage-regulat: A 7806 voltage regulator delivers roughly 6 V on the test bench, including the one suspected in an Aiwa repair. The fault must be elsewhere. ⚡
/hakko-808-desoldering-tool-demo/: The Hakko 808 makes removing a 100 uF through-hole capacitor delightfully easy. Heat, suction, and no half-hour battle with desoldering braid. 🔧
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-01-01-mainboa: An Aiwa CSD-GM1 boom box mainboard gets a sea of fresh capacitors and a 7806 regulator. A hairline PCB crack needs checking, and testing is still ahead. 🔧
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-part-2-volume: After recapping an Aiwa CSD-GM1, the radio plays and the CD mechanism shows signs of life. The low-volume problem and unreliable power remain unsolved. 🎵
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-part-3-review: An Aiwa Mega-CD's CD player unexpectedly plays 13 tracks, but bumps, wavy video and missing Game Unit power keep the repair saga alive. 🔧
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-part-4-tracin: A missing 8 V rail leads to a suspicious transistor stage on the Aiwa CSD-GM1. One board has 7.7 V in and almost nothing out, but the cause isn't confirmed. ⚡
/x0xb0x-10-adafruit-edition-progress-rep: SuperNick's Adafruit x0xb0x takes another step towards making music. Sawtooth waveform tests are promising, but the synth isn't finished yet. 🎵
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-02-01-rev-2-mainbo: The cracked revision 2 Aiwa CSD-GM1 board gets a recap, but differing capacitor values and old trace repairs keep the parts list growing. 🔧
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-game-unit-eprom-pr: An erased and reprogrammed 27C1024 EPROM brings the Aiwa Mega-CD BIOS screen back to life. Those earlier socket and trace repairs might be paying off. 💾
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-unit-02-mainboard-: Both Aiwa Mega-CD Game Units produce video on the same revision 2 mainboard. The BIOS works, but interference and missing amplified audio still need attention. 🎮
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-unit-02-mic-amp-bo: Two tiny broken traces on an Aiwa microphone amplifier board finally get bridged, restoring amplified sound. Naturally a separate volume problem appears. 🔧
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-game-unit-in-: The Aiwa Mega-CD Game Unit runs Mega Drive cartridges without the boombox when powered from a properly regulated 5 V supply. One fewer enormous bench setup! 🎮
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-unit-01-mainb: Another recap of the Aiwa CSD-GM1 revision 1 board reveals a mislabeled replacement capacitor. Always read the markings, even when the parts look identical. 🔧
/super-nintendo-snes-cartridge-battery-h: An NHL '96 SNES cartridge gets a CR2032 battery-holder experiment for an EarthBound project. The holder works in theory, but the shell won't close. 💾
/x0xb0x-10-adafruit-edition-assembly-com: SuperNick's x0xb0x is fully assembled but silent. A temporary voltage test coaxes out some sound, pointing towards the audio circuitry. Repair still pending. 🎵
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-unit-02-volume-boa: The Aiwa CSD-GM1's left channel keeps playing when the volume is turned down. A troublesome seven-pin B50K control becomes the next suspect. 🎵
/subscribe-today-version-10/: The first RetroJunkie YouTube channel trailer invites everyone to browse an alarming number of videos about retro computers, games and hardware chaos. 📺
/console-collection-overview-28th-august: August 2013 brings more Sega consoles, Super Nintendos, PlayStations and stray Xboxes than one home should reasonably contain. Another collection tour! 🎮
/burning-out-250ma-fuses-in-slow-motion/: Watch a few tiny 250 mA fuses give up in gloriously grainy 320×240 slow motion. The power adapter's rating isn't the actual fuse current. ⚡
/bob-parkers-anatek-blue-esr-meter-assem: A DIY AnaTek Blue ESR meter gets assembled and tested on old Aiwa capacitors. Some readings are surprisingly normal, even on parts that look dreadful. 🔧
/cleaning-game-cartridges-with-a-pencil-: A pencil eraser makes grubby Super Nintendo cartridge contacts look shiny again. It also removes material, so this isn't something to overdo. 🎮
/dogs-20-revenge-of-the-dogs/: Pepper, Coco and Prinny return in Dogs 2.0, a feature-length extravaganza of running around, pats on the head and perhaps even sitting on command. 🐶
/cleaning-game-cartridge-slots-with-isop: An old Mega Drive 2 cartridge slot gets cleaned using high-purity isopropyl alcohol and a cloth-wrapped card. The grime coming out is rather impressive. 🎮
/catastrophic-multimeter-failure-with-ai: My cheap multimeter probes decide to fall apart mid-Aiwa repair, leaving the power-supply detective work on hold. Naturally there's also a random cat. 🐈
/sega-mega-drive-shelf-quick-look-and-ne: An old Sega Mega Drive shelf overview has vanished from the archive, leaving only a substitute devkit image and a complaint about the neighbours' bongo drums. 🥁
/aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-volume-board-repai: Contact cleaner reduces crackle in the Aiwa CSD-GM1 volume control but doesn't fix its faulty left channel. Time to take the seven-pin control apart. 🔧
/aiwa-sega-mega-cd-csd-gm1-tape-deck-tes: An Aiwa Mega-CD cassette deck finally plays music through both speakers, while the radio still fails and the other tape mechanism needs mechanical repairs. 📼
/blown-capacitors-in-a-netcomm-np285-tur: Two NetComm NP285 HomePlug ethernet adapters reveal very different capacitor choices. One has bulging SamXon parts; the cause is not yet established. 🔌
/cooking-with-mcretro-creative-custard/: Cooking with McRetro combines thick custard and an unreasonable quantity of chocolate chips. One forgotten spoon and a questionable dinner choice later... 🍮
/super-mario-2-standing-on-the-shoulders: Super Mario Bros. 2 on Super Mario All-Stars has me standing on enemies instead of flattening them. Why did Nintendo change the rules? 🎮
/the-weasel-skink-lizard-up-close-and-pe: A cold and sluggish weasel skink spends the night in a luxury DVD-spindle shelter before being released. Also, 500 YouTube subscribers! 🦎
/ym3438-on-the-sega-teradrive-sonic-spin: The Sega TeraDrive's original YM3438 keeps Sonic Spinball music playing after the options menu. A modified Mega Drive's audio issue remains a mystery. 🎵
/sega-master-system-converter-experiment: A Master System converter won't physically fit the Sega TeraDrive. An Action Replay extension and Mega EverDrive produce black screens, not Wonder Boy. 🎮
/collection-dilemma-where-to-draw-the-li: How many retro consoles are too many? A crowded Sega collection prompts some difficult decisions about duplicates, motherboard revisions and shelf space. 🎮
/27c801-eprom-snes-donor-cartridge-demo-: A modified SNES donor cartridge boots Super Bomberman 2 from a programmed 27C801 EPROM. Crooked wires aside, the proof of concept works! 💾
/creating-snes-cartridges-with-tsop40-fl: Two sacrificial sports-game cartridges become SNES flash-memory experiments, with TSOP40 adapters, sockets and a lot of fine-pitch soldering ahead. 🎮
/gq-4x-flashing-earthbound-onto-tsop40-a: An AM29F032B TSOP40 chip finally accepts an EarthBound image through the GQ-4X after a reseat. Programming verified; cartridge assembly is a separate job. 💾
/removing-a-snes-cartridge-battery-a-bad: Removing an old SNES cartridge battery turns into a burnt-finger adventure, followed by the discovery that the new holder is too tall. Not a good bench day. 🔧
/sega-dreamcast-arcade-sticks-difference: Two Sega Dreamcast arcade sticks look nearly identical until you inspect the logos and labels. PAL and NTSC manufacturing clues remain a guessing game. 🎮
/aiwa-csd-ex80-vs-aiwa-mega-cd-csd-gm1-d: An ordinary Aiwa CSD-EX80 looks suspiciously like the CSD-GM1 Mega-CD boombox. Its working volume control, tape deck and aerial make it a promising donor. 📻
/delonghi-tasciugo-dds30combi-dehumidifi: A DeLonghi dehumidifier tries to rescue a house full of cardboard and retro hardware from humidity. The noise and electricity use are less impressive. 💧
/removing-a-snes-cartridge-battery-and-t: Lower-profile SNES cartridge battery holders look more promising, alongside new TSOP40 flash adapters. No triumphant installation to report just yet. 💾
/super-nintendo-serial-up12144537-capaci: A supposedly spare-parts SNES UP12144537 actually works! New capacitors go in, while its horribly yellowed case awaits a more colourful future. 🎮
/snes-spray-painting-when-retrobright-is: Two brittle, yellowed Super Nintendo shells get prepared for red and black vinyl spray paint. Early coats look promising, with reassembly still ahead. 🎨
/sony-playstation-modchip-programming-fa: A PIC12C508A refuses to verify properly after programming for a PlayStation modchip. The configuration or calibration may be wrong; no working chip yet. 🔧
/sony-playstation-1-modchip-installation: A PlayStation SCPH-9002 modchip installation goes sideways when a tiny surface-mount part comes off the board. An accidental lesson in soldering restraint. 🎮
/circuit-bending-vram-on-a-sega-mega-dri: Deliberately bridging Mega Drive 2 VRAM signals produces wild Zero Wing and Sonic glitches. Hard to tell which faults were already there, though. 🎮
/lets-sing-karaoke-pac-panic-1993/: Pac-Panic karaoke with Jason and some questionable singing turns a Friday into a Sega-flavoured music video. Songwriting remains harder than it looks. 🎤
/sega-mega-drive-2-video-distortion-seri: Mega Drive 2 serial 440005313 produces corrupted video even after a DC-in repair. Pressing on a Sega chip temporarily steadies the picture. A clue, not a fix. 🔧
/voltage-drop-on-a-sega-mega-drive-2/: Turning down a Mega Drive 2's supply voltage makes its audio fade, colours vanish and games crash. Familiar symptoms from the Aiwa Mega-CD experiments. ⚡
/replacing-the-video-encoder-chip-and-av: A Mega Drive 2 gets a replacement video encoder and AV socket, but the original distortion stubbornly survives. At least the footage is mercifully shortened. 🔧
/replacing-vram-on-a-sega-mega-drive-2/: Replacing the VRAM on Mega Drive 2 serial 440005313 requires some heroic soldering and produces plenty of new glitches, but not the repair I wanted. 🔧
/psio-prototype-hardware-11-overview/: An early PSIO prototype revision 1.1 arrives with a Cyclone III FPGA and MicroSD slot. A hardware tour first, actual PlayStation game tests later. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-dance-dance: PSIO prototype 1.1 loads Dance Dance Revolution 5th Mix, but some music goes missing and RGB gives a blank screen. Composite works in monochrome. Fancy footwork optional. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-tekken-3/: Tekken 3 starts loading on the PSIO 1.1 prototype, then refuses to progress beyond early activity. One sound effect and a lot of waiting. More testing needed. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-test-station-setup-ov: A PAL SCPH-5502 without its CD drive becomes the PSIO 1.1 test station, complete with XRGB-mini and PC-based loading. Let the game compatibility chaos begin! 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-final-fanta: Final Fantasy VII gets a promising PSIO 1.1 test, with opening scenes, sound, battles and reactor escape all working. Pizza helps, naturally. Not a full-game test. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-r4-ridge-ra: R4: Ridge Racer Type 4 runs in Time Attack on PSIO 1.1, but Grand Prix hangs and some audio is absent. The driving, meanwhile, is alarmingly creative. 🏎️
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-the-legend-: The Legend of Dragoon refuses to progress on PSIO prototype 1.1, even after restarts and a European version test. Another compatibility mystery for the list. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-metal-gear-: Metal Gear Solid runs nicely through the early stages on PSIO prototype 1.1. Snake is sneaky; the person holding the controller is considerably less so. 🎮
Metal Gear Solid: Integral boots and plays well on PSIO 1.1, with English voices and extra Japanese features. Sadly, the guards still keep catching me. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-medievil-ii: MediEvil II loads on PSIO 1.1 with missing audio and stalls at a ghostly sequence. Avoiding that moment gets further, but compatibility is far from perfect. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-chrono-trig: Chrono Trigger 1.0 reaches the year 600 AD on PSIO 1.1, with working gameplay and music but silent opening FMV. Time travel seems easier than troubleshooting. ⏳
Chrono Trigger 1.1 repeatedly hangs at a black screen on PSIO 1.1, while version 1.0 gets further. A strangely specific early-prototype compatibility problem. 🎮
/supercic-installation-notes-snsp-cpu-02: SuperCIC installation notes for a PAL SNSP-CPU-02 with F413A, including PIC16F630 wiring and photographs. Useful reference, not a complete standalone guide. 🔧
/cuckoo-bird-flying-short-story/: A cuckoo bird gets a DIY perch made from an old Sega Activator box. Finally, a practical use for one of Sega's most spectacularly awkward accessories! 🐦
/my-new-plants/: Some boysenberry plants arrive with grand plans for a berry hedge. First I need to keep them alive. Also, Final Cut Pro apparently lets me set plants on fire. 🌱
/reducing-the-vertical-bar-band-on-the-s: Two 220 uF capacitors reduce the SNES vertical bar, but a wiring mishap costs more than fifteen hours of EarthBound saves. Cleaner video, very expensive lesson. 🎮
/sony-playstation-1-eject-button-mainten: A sticky original PlayStation eject button gets cleaned and lightly greased. It finally opens and closes smoothly, without the usual wiggle and encouragement. 🔧
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-crash-team-: Crash Team Racing runs nicely on the early PSIO prototype, even letting me win a race. Working hardware and competent driving in one video? Unprecedented! 🏁
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-star-ocean-: Star Ocean: The Second Story gets a promising PSIO 1.1 test, including FMV sound, music and battles. Unfortunately I keep forgetting to use a weapon. 🎮
/sony-ps-one-laser-assembly-disassembly-: A Sony PS one replacement laser mechanism gets taken apart, revealing tiny guide pieces and dubious spindle hubs. Not every cheap replacement fits as advertised. 🔧
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-final-fanta: Final Fantasy IX runs nicely on PSIO 1.1 until I pull out the microSD card mid-game. Unsurprisingly it doesn't recover, and I hadn't saved my progress. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-resident-ev: Resident Evil refuses to run properly on the early PSIO prototype, even after multiple restarts. No B-grade voice acting for me today. Prototype woes! 🧟
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-tekken-3-de: A debug bootloader gets Tekken 3 further on PSIO 1.1 than before, but the game runs painfully slowly. Progress, yes. Playable fighting, not quite. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-crash-bandi: Crash Bandicoot boots and plays beautifully on PSIO 1.1, complete with cutscene sound and save support. Sadly it can't prevent me jumping onto TNT crates. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-crash-bash/: Crash Bash boots on an early PSIO revision with music and playable minigames. The prototype behaves; my inability to follow the instructions is another matter. 🎮
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-rage-racer/: Rage Racer plays on PSIO 1.1, but the background music is missing and some scenery looks odd. I can hit every barrier at impressive speed, though! 🏎️
/psio-prototype-11-game-demo-tenchu-stea: Tenchu starts its opening video on PSIO prototype 1.1, minus the soundtrack, then stops at a black screen. So much for ninja stealth practice. 🎮
/sony-ps-one-replacement-laser-assembly-: Out of eight cheap PS one laser assemblies, only two seem to hold their spindle hubs properly. One pickup reads discs, but the mechanical quality is dreadful. 💿
/cleaning-a-sega-master-system-controlle: Master System controller Button 2 stops misbehaving after a clean with methylated spirits. The rubber contacts survive, and Wonder Boy gets another outing. 🎮
/sega-master-system-ii-in-8-bit-mayhem/: A rescued Sega Master System II stubbornly shows a black screen instead of Alex Kidd. Corrosion, composite video and a spare encoder offer no easy answer. 🔧
/australian-sega-oddities-rarities-fatal: An unusual Australian Sega Saturn controller and a PAL Fatal Fury 2 cartridge get a closer look. Sega Ozisoft certainly knew how to make odd accessories. 🎮
/lunchbeat-1-bit-groovebox-by-buranelect: A tiny ATmega328P-based Lunchbeat groovebox makes a glorious racket. The improvised prototype works, and a proper printed circuit board is on the wish list. 🎵
An ATmega328P, six buttons, five knobs and a forest of loose wires become a working Lunchbeat 1-bit groovebox prototype. Messy, noisy and beautiful. 🎶
/sega-dreamcast-microphone-on-canon-eos-: A Sega Dreamcast Planet Ring microphone gets pressed into service on a Canon EOS 600D. Mono audio goes to both channels; the next microphone may be better. 🎤
/sega-saturn-pack-in-games-from-november: A sealed 1996 Sega Saturn pack-in bundle yields Virtua Fighter 2, Virtua Cop, Daytona USA and a glorious promotional poster. What do I do with the box? 🎮
/sony-playstation-2-laser-replacement-fa: A PlayStation 2 laser swap spirals into 24 minutes of incompatible mechanisms, screws and disappointment. Perhaps checking pickup models first would've helped. 🔧
The short version of a failed PlayStation 2 optical pickup repair features levering, one ominous crunch and a shower of broken parts. No victory music today. 💥
/sony-playstation-2-slim-laser-assembly-: Two faulty PS2 Slim consoles donate enough parts for one machine that reads PS1 games. A mysterious green picture turns out to be the video output setting. 🎮
/xrg-xtreme-retro-gaming-now-closed/: Xtreme Retro Gaming was a wonderfully chaotic side channel for badly played games and questionable commentary. Sadly, it eventually closed through neglect. 🎮
/sega-master-system-reassembly-in-high-s: A Sega Master System goes back together at high speed. The actual console still needs repair, but at least the screws are finally where they belong. 🔧
/upcoming-microsoft-xbox-softmod-tsop-mo: Two original Xbox consoles await softmod and TSOP experiments, with Splinter Cell, a USB cable hack and a questionable hard drive. What could go wrong? 🎮
/snes-controller-pad-inspection-and-clea: A genuine SNES controller gets fresh button membranes salvaged from a dreadful three-dollar knockoff. EarthBound feels much better after the clean-up. 🎮
/birds-in-buckets-in-backyards/: A little honeyeater gets rescued from a water-filled bucket, dried off and released. Then the bucket gets tipped over. Hopefully that's the last one! 🐦
/seagate-20gb-hard-drive-dissected/: A dead Seagate 20 GB hard drive gets dissected for science. Shiny platter, tiny heads and a reminder that backups matter more than shiny metal. 💾
/sega-teradrive-sped-up-reassembly/: The Sega TeraDrive front panel goes back together in speedy fashion after a Yamaha sound-chip investigation. More vintage screws, less vintage patience. 🔧
/mcretro-friends-making-cupcakes-version: Cupcake attempt 1.0 combines too many eggs, plain flour and questionable measurements into something flat and omelette-like. Version 2.0 is required! 🧁
SuperNick and I return with self-raising flour, fewer eggs and a slightly improved recipe. The second cupcake attempt actually tastes like cupcakes! 🧁
/snes-cartridge-backup-battery-holders/: Finding a low-profile SNES cartridge battery holder becomes a saga of shell clearance, awkward pins and green Kynar wire. A Panasonic part finally fits. 💾
/subscribe-today-version-20/: RetroJunkie's second channel trailer celebrates more subscribers, impending doom and videos with SuperNick. Don't forget to subscribe before the gates open! 🔥
/super-nes-spray-painting-completed/: Two badly yellowed SNES shells are now an extremely sassy red-and-black combination. Some paint still scratches and a few grey details remain, but look at them! 🎨
/two-faulty-sega-saturn-sophia-developme: Two more UK Sega Saturn Sophia development kits join the bench, both without video. Three Sophias, six SH-2 boards and a rather intimidating repair queue. 🔧
/pic12f629-blinking-led-test-and-mccain-: A PIC12F629 happily blinks a two-colour LED from a Nokia charger, but still refuses to verify the PlayStation modchip firmware. Also, McCain Pizza Pockets. 💡
/sony-playstation-1-modchip-installation: PlayStation SCPH-9002 modchip testing improves after discovering badly burned CDs. Verify your discs before blaming the chip! Composite video still has issues. 💿
After earlier disasters, MultiMode3 finally runs on a PlayStation SCPH-9002 using a PIC12F629 and some remarkably untidy wiring. Blu Tack included. 🎮
/snes-supercic-switchless-modchip-instal: A SuperCIC switchless mod goes into a PAL Super Nintendo with a PIC16F630, lifted CIC pins and tiny PPU connections. Solder bridges keep things interesting. 🔧
/snes-supercic-switchless-modchip-the-te: The SuperCIC finally changes a PAL SNES between 50 Hz and 60 Hz. John Madden sounds hilariously fast, although the first tests need a little tidying. 🎮
/sony-ps-one-onechip-modchip-introductio: ONEchip promises import support for a PAL PS one SCPH-102, where MultiMode3 alone can't bypass the extra boot-ROM check. Wrong PICs delay installation. 🎮
/snes-supercic-switchless-modchip-more-t: A homemade SNES cartridge without its original CIC runs EarthBound under SuperCIC testing. Fourteen hours of quality assurance later, I may need sleep. 🎮
/cleaning-the-sony-ps-one-eject-button-m: A sticky PS one eject button gets dismantled and cleaned, revealing something resembling chocolate syrup. Happily it works again without extra grease. 🔧
/earthbound-completed-on-nintendo-ds-lit: After losing my SNES EarthBound saves, I finish the game on a Nintendo DS Lite with SNEmulDS. Slightly glitchy music, very late nights, actual victory! 🎮
/sony-playstation-junk-cd-decks-partial-: Cheap replacement PlayStation disc hubs keep breaking, but two plastic cards help lift one intact. Getting the spindle height right is still another job. 💿
/sony-playstation-junk-cd-decks-the-disc: A pile of replacement PlayStation CD decks looks promising until their short spindle shafts let the plastic hubs fall off. Quality control strikes again. 💿
/sony-ps-one-laser-replacement-with-extr: A Sony PS one optical pickup swap becomes an adventure in rails, little plastic guides and stubborn gears. The mechanics are almost more trouble than the laser. 🔧
/the-theme-from-sega-channel-japan/: The Japanese Sega Channel theme gets a direct Mega Drive Model 1 recording and slideshow. Vintage game-service music, captured on a Canon EOS 600D. 🎵
/water-damaged-sony-ps-one-repair-attemp: A water-damaged PS one gets a replacement power switch, cleaned connectors and revived controller ports. The CD drive still refuses to read discs. 🔧
/sega-mega-drive-genesis-cart-dumping-vi: Making a Mega Drive cartridge dumper with a Mega-CD, controller port 2 and a PC parallel cable sounds brilliant. The first home-made transfer doesn't work. 💾
A proper Tototek cable and bidirectional parallel port finally let a Mega-CD dump PAL Fatal Fury 2. Sometimes buying the right cable is worth it! 💾
The Sega CD Transfer Suite dumps Sonic through a Mega Drive controller port and a PC parallel connection. ECP/EPP settings had been the real nuisance. 💾
/japanese-sega-channel-adapter-first-loo: Two Japanese Sega Channel adapters arrive for inspection. One has an angry-looking startup screen, a catchy tune and an enormous casing. BIOS dumping awaits. 🎮
/japanese-sega-channel-adapter-second-lo: A second Japanese Sega Channel look reveals different labels, a menu button and a stubborn cable search. Without Japanese cable TV, there's only so far to go. 📺
/socketing-the-sega-channel-adapter-bios: Socketing the Japanese Sega Channel adapter's BIOS makes future dumps easier. The menus and Sonic animation still work afterwards. Not bad at all! 🔧
/dumping-the-japanese-sega-channel-bios-: A Japanese Sega Channel ROM is removed for dumping, but repeated reads don't agree. Having a file is not the same as having a reliable preservation copy. 💾
Recognisable Sega Channel BIOS text appears after byte swapping, but repeated dumps have different checksums. GQ-4X, why must you do this to me? 💾
Finally! Tweaking the GQ-4X device VCC setting produces repeated matching Sega Channel BIOS checksums. Dr. Eggfan and a little persistence save the day. 💾
/happy-christmas-and-a-merry-new-year-ce: Happy Christmas from the land down under! Moving house, terrible upload speeds and noisy neighbours put the retro videos on pause for a while. 🎄
/programming-atmel-avr-chips-with-pickit: A PICkit 2 can program supported Atmel AVR chips through AVRDUDE on a Mac, including the Lunchbeat's ATmega328P. Compiling it is another adventure. 💻
/cooking-with-mcretro-a-quick-doughnut-f: Doughnuts without enough cinnamon sugar? The solution is revolutionary: sprinkle on more caster sugar. Cooking with McRetro reaches new culinary heights! 🍩
/a-quick-doughnut-fix-behind-the-scenes-: A one-minute doughnut video somehow requires 16 minutes of editing in Final Cut Pro X on an old Core 2 Duo Mac. Behind the scenes of great nonsense. 🎬
/blue-spark-digital-microphone-disassemb: A $250 Blue Spark Digital microphone has a loose connector, awkward stand and questionable internal assembly. The sound is decent, when it stays connected. 🎤
/blue-yeti-microphone-unboxing/: The enormous Blue Yeti arrives from the Apple Store after a disappointing Blue Spark Digital. First impressions are solid, but audio testing comes later. 🎤
